rationale: Interpreted the BatchApplyCh receipt and requested the correction it needs. The receipt reproduces the VerifyLeader strand and the unbuffered Barrier/Apply contrast, and its new batched cases show the config flip: with applyCh buffered, Barrier answered 4, 5 and 6 of eight post-shutdown calls and Apply 4, 4 and 3, leaving the rest unanswered, which pins the mechanism to channel buffering. The declared comparisons for those cases came back unresolved because the batched cases share trial and kind with the unbuffered ones, making the admitting setup event ambiguous, so this update both records the event-level values and submits a revision that gives the batched cases distinct trial identifiers and carries batch_apply_ch on the setup event as well. No earlier receipt is withdrawn; the racing form stays as the timing-dependent manifestation.

interpretations.rationale: The question is whether a future handed back by VerifyLeader, Barrier or Apply around Shutdown can be left permanently uncompleted, and three retained runs now answer it for VerifyLeader while showing that the same strand follows channel buffering rather than the API. In this run the VerifyLeader strand reproduced (result events at parsed indices 1, 7 and 13, comparison 4 holds), and so did the contrast: with the default unbuffered applyCh, Barrier and Apply answered every one of their eight post-shutdown calls in all three trials (indices 3, 9, 15 and 5, 11, 17; comparisons 2 and 3 hold). The new batched cases, where BatchApplyCh buffers applyCh to MaxAppendEntries, show the flip: Barrier answered 4, 5 and 6 of eight post-shutdown calls (indices 25, 29, 33) and Apply answered 4, 4 and 3 (indices 27, 31, 35), leaving 4, 3 and 2 and then 4, 4 and 5 futures unanswered after 500ms, in each case with the rest answered by 'raft is already shutdown'. The mechanism is therefore pinned by a configuration change: only the channel's buffering differs between the answered and the stranded cases, since Config.BatchApplyCh exists exactly to buffer applyCh and its own comment warns that it breaks the timeout guarantee on Apply. The declared comparisons for those new cases came back unresolved rather than satisfied, because the batched cases reuse the same trial and kind as the unbuffered ones, so the setup event that admits each result event is ambiguous; the event values themselves are recorded and decisive, and a corrected revision that gives the batched cases distinct trial identifiers and records batch_apply_ch on the setup event as well is submitted with this update. What the three runs together establish is narrower and firmer than the first account: the racing phase is the fragile part (9 and 41 of 64 in the first run, 0 of 128 in the two later ones), while the post-shutdown phase is stable, and the defect is confined to call kinds whose channel is buffered, with VerifyLeader always in that set and the apply path only when BatchApplyCh is enabled.
counterevidence: The racing form did not reproduce in the two later runs (0 of 128 per case), so the earlier 9 and 41 are a timing-dependent manifestation rather than a rate.
Without BatchApplyCh, Barrier and Apply never stranded a future in any run (0 of 192, 0 of 384 and 0 of 384 attempts), so the defect does not touch the default apply path.

The batched comparisons in this receipt are unresolved rather than satisfied because of an ambiguity in the harness admission, so the config-flip result rests on the recorded event values, which the corrected revision re-measures with unambiguous identities.
Every call that was answered returned success or the documented 'raft is already shutdown' error, so no completed call carries a wrong outcome.
limitations: The batched counts come from three trials of eight post-shutdown calls each (Barrier 4, 5, 6 answered; Apply 4, 4, 3 answered) in one execution, so they bound the mechanism rather than a population rate.
The strand is classified by a 500ms window; permanence is inferred from the source, since no reader of the affected channel remains and these futures have no shutdown channel.
Single-voter node with in-memory transport and 50ms timeouts; no peer round trip or networked shutdown is involved.
The comparison records for the batched cases are unresolved in this receipt for a harness reason (ambiguous admission), which the submitted revision corrects rather than the account working around.
interpretations.joint_history: This receipt is the third revision of the same harness lineage: b2ccc787c9384b008b5f9c668746f760-experiment issued 64 calls with a 1500ms window, 49fa455b2fe94d53ab6fed2fad19ce33-experiment raised that to 128 calls and 4000ms and added the post-shutdown phase, and 3b7823e321e048b88feb0bab3b79b2bd-experiment added the BatchApplyCh cases and the batch_apply_ch field. Event names, case kinds and the meaning of every carried field are unchanged across the three, and the earlier receipts remain the evidence for the racing form.

experiment.revision_reason: The batched cases were admitted ambiguously because they shared trial and kind with the unbuffered cases and the setup event did not carry batch_apply_ch, so their comparisons were unresolved. This revision gives the batched cases trial identifiers 100 to 102 and records batch_apply_ch on the setup event as well as the result event, so each result event can be admitted by exactly one setup event. Cases, event names and measured fields are otherwise unchanged.

scope.description: Run the shutdown probe for VerifyLeader, Barrier and Apply with the default unbuffered applyCh and for Barrier and Apply with BatchApplyCh enabled, three trials each, recording racing and post-shutdown completion counts and the batch_apply_ch flag, with a no-shutdown control; the batched cases use distinct trial identifiers so each result event is admitted by a single setup event.
assumptions: BatchApplyCh is a supported option whose documented effect is to buffer applyCh to MaxAppendEntries and to break the timeout guarantee on Apply.
MaxAppendEntries (the default) is large enough that the post-shutdown sends never block, so the buffered send stays selectable exactly as verifyCh's does.
Single-voter node, in-memory transport, 50ms timeouts, one process.
excluded: Multi-node behaviour and buffer sizes small enough to block the sends.

experiment.prefix: Each case starts one real Raft instance with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, bootstrapped as a single Voter with HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 50ms and BatchApplyCh set only for the batched cases, and waits until it reports Leader. It emits assurance_shutdown_setup carrying trial, kind, shutdown, batch_apply_ch, the call counts and the window, then issues 128 calls of the chosen kind from separate goroutines, each waiting on Error() with a 4000ms deadline, and in the shutdown cases calls Shutdown() from a goroutine 2ms later. After Shutdown returns it issues 8 further calls one at a time with a 500ms wait each and emits assurance_shutdown_result with the racing counts, the post-phase counts and histograms, the shutdown error, the node state and batch_apply_ch. Batched barrier and apply cases use trial identifiers 100 to 102 so their setup and result events are distinguishable from the unbuffered ones. The harness is TestAssuranceShutdownFutureCompletion.

comparisons.description: Barrier with BatchApplyCh: at least one post-shutdown call left unanswered, which would confirm the strand follows buffering.
Apply with BatchApplyCh: same prediction for the documented buffered configuration.
Barrier with the default unbuffered applyCh: every post-shutdown call answered.
Apply with the default unbuffered applyCh: same contrast.
VerifyLeader, whose channel is always buffered: the strand re-measured alongside the batched cases.
